title: One Model, Two Precisions: Does Disagreement Between Quantized Copies Tell You When a Small Model Is Wrong?
abstract: arXiv:2611.16478v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Local language models often exist at several precisions, and quantization is known to change individual answers. This study asks whether the disagreement between two precisions of the same weights, an 8-bit copy that answers and a lower-precision copy that reads the same prompt, works as a per-question error score for abstention, escalation and re-asking. The cost is one extra forward pass over fewer bytes, with no sampling and no training. We simulate round-to-nearest quantization with per-group scales (3 to 6 bits, groups of 32 to 256) on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B and score 8,398 multiple-choice questions from ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MMLU and HellaSwag subsets. Error detection is measured by AUROC, risk-coverage curves and ECE on a held-out half, with paired bootstrap intervals over questions. For Qwen3-0.6B, the entropy of the 8-bit answer reaches AUROC 0.682; the best disagreement score, selected on a development half, reaches 0.684

translated_title: 一个模型，两种精度：量化副本之间的分歧能否告诉你小模型何时出错？
translated_abstract: 本地语言模型通常以多种精度存在，而量化已知会改变模型的个别回答。本研究探讨同一权重的两种精度之间的分歧——一个负责回答的8比特副本和一个读取相同提示的低精度副本——能否作为逐问题的错误评分，用于弃答、升级和重新提问。其成本仅为对更少字节数进行一次额外的前向传播，无需采样，也无需训练。我们在Qwen3-0.6B和Qwen3-1.7B上模拟了带分组缩放的舍入到最近邻量化（3至6比特，每组32至256），并对来自ARC-Easy、ARC-Challenge、MMLU和HellaSwag子集的8,398道选择题进行评分。错误检测通过AUROC、风险-覆盖曲线以及在留出一半数据上的ECE来衡量，并采用基于问题的成对自助法区间进行统计评估。对于Qwen3-0.6B，8比特回答的熵达到AUROC 0.682；在开发集一半数据上选出的最佳分歧评分达到0.684。
tldr: 该论文提出一种无需训练、仅需一次额外前向传播的方法，利用同一权重8比特与低精度量化副本之间的分歧作为逐题错误评分信号来检测小语言模型的错误，但实验发现其最佳分歧评分（AUROC 0.684）仅与8比特回答的熵（0.682）表现相当。
en_tdlr: This study proposes a training-free method requiring only one extra forward pass that uses the disagreement between an 8-bit and a lower-precision quantized copy of the same weights as a per-question error score for detecting when small language models are wrong, finding that the best disagreement score (AUROC 0.684) performs comparably to the entropy of the 8-bit answer (0.682).
